observation.visible_scene: A close side view of an osprey partly submerged in calm water, with a blurred green-and-tan grassy bank filling the background and a 'maramedia' logo in the top-right corner. The bird faces left; a fan of water droplets sprays around its rear (right side of frame) throughout.
visible_changes: At t=0 the head and neck stand upright above the surface and one wing is raised high, angled toward the upper right.

From t=0 to about t=0.88 the raised wing stays near-vertical while its primary feathers splay and the wing tip drifts from a rightward angle toward straight up; the head remains up and the right-side spray continues.
From about t=0.96 to t=1.6 the raised wing rotates forward and down over the back, the body pitches downward, and the head dips until it is partly hidden behind the wing.

From about t=1.68 to t=2.4 the bird levels out: the head reappears above the wing line facing left, the body sits low, and the wings extend sideways toward the left while the spray persists at the right.

From about t=2.5 to t=3.2 the body tilts again with its rear toward the splash, the head drops out of view behind the dark back/shoulder, and the leftward-extended wing stays spread; the posture is more horizontal and lower in the water than at the start.

Persistent features across all frames: white head plumage with a dark eye-stripe and yellow eye (when the head is visible), barred dark-brown upper-wing feathers, white underparts, and the continuous right-side water spray.
The background grass line and the bird's apparent size shift slightly over the clip, but it is not clear whether this is camera motion or the bird moving through the water.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the bird has captured prey or is empty-handed (no fish or object is visible in this excerpt).
What produced the initial splash and whether the bird is taking off, struggling, or feeding.
The bird's state before t=0 and after t=3.2 (the segment's ends are arbitrary crop boundaries).
uncertain_details: Direction and magnitude of any camera pan/zoom versus bird translation.
Exact position of the head in the final frames (it is occluded by the wing/back).
Whether the white patch visible near the top in the last frames is the head, nape, or shoulder.
